record_body:
Account summary
- Devtools vendor building an SDK + hosted UI for "bring-your-own-model" code assistant workflows. Partner-ish angle: they may list Redwood as an inference option inside their platform + co-market if perf is strong.
- Entered via PLG: self-serve signup + retargeting. Now sales-engaged after asking for benchmark proof and Dedicated pricing.

Firmographics
- Company: Kiteworks DevTools (kiteworks.dev)
- Size: 51–200; NA HQ; sells into startups + mid-market engineering teams
- Buying pattern: developer-led evaluation, then central platform approval

Current stage
- Evaluation: they have a working prototype, want to run a short POC (2–3 weeks) but requesting benchmark substantiation first.

Primary contacts (per notes)
- "Sam" (Head of Product) – cares about positioning and partner story
- "Irene" (Staff Eng) – cares about latency/streaming stability, SDK ergonomics
- "Mark" (Security) – asked about retention, audit logs, and KMS

Use case / workload
- Code assistant + doc-aware chat for IDE/web (mix of chat + retrieval + summarization)
- High usage variance during product launches and conference demos (spiky traffic)
- Streaming is mandatory for UX; tool/function calling likely within 2 quarters
- Model mix: wants freedom to switch open models; asked if Redwood can provide fallback routing across model versions

Key requirements / questions
- Performance
  - Target: "feels instant" streaming; they cited wanting first token < ~250–400ms in the common case (not contractual yet)
  - Interested in Redwood benchmarks and methodology (hardware, batch settings, sequence lengths)
  - Asked for proof on cost per 1M tokens comparisons ("don’t need exact dollars, need directional")
- Product
  - Wants a clear quickstart landing page they can point their developers to (copy/paste curl + TS/Python)
  - Wants console visibility: token cost + latency breakdowns for demos
- Security / compliance
  - Needs SOC 2 for vendor review (they’re SOC 2 themselves; want to avoid weak links)
  - Retention controls: asked how long prompts/completions are retained, how to disable retention, and whether logs contain payloads
  - KMS: asked if keys can be customer-managed for Dedicated/VPC later
  - Audit logging: needs access logs for admin actions + key creation
- Commercial
  - Hosted API okay for evaluation; expects Dedicated baseline capacity once they roll out to more customers
  - Wants a pricing "floor" for Dedicated (min commit) and what burst looks like

Retargeting / marketing touches (tracked)
- 2025-01-16: LinkedIn retargeting click (campaign: lifecycle_sprint_dev_nonactivated_v1). Landed on quickstart variant w/ benchmarks section.
- 2025-01-18: Returned via direct; created API key; did not complete first streaming call (saw errors per their note).
- 2025-01-22: Clicked "Benchmarks" link from email follow-up; replied asking for "source of truth" benchmark writeup and reproducible setup.

Timeline & recent activity
- 2025-01-09 (Avery): Inbound created from self-serve signup; flagged as potential partner due to devtools category.
- 2025-01-16 (Marketing Ops): Retargeting touch recorded; UTM present on landing page session.
- 2025-01-18 (Support via chat widget): User asked where to find streaming example; pointed to SDK README + console docs. (No Jira created.)
- 2025-01-23 (Avery): Discovery call scheduled; asked Ethan Wallace to prep benchmark substantiation.
- 2025-01-27 (Call / Fireflies ff_905218): Discussed use case + perf expectations; asked for: (1) benchmark link, (2) Dedicated ballpark, (3) retention controls summary.
- 2025-02-03 (Call / Fireflies ff_905401): Technical Qs on routing/fallback and rate limits; they want to test 2 models + streaming stability.
- 2025-02-06 (Email): Avery sent draft partner one-pager + asked for target launch date; they replied "we need benchmark proof before we put Redwood in front of customers".

Sales notes (verbatim-ish snippets)
- "If you can show us consistent streaming and good p95, we can make Redwood the default inference option for our hosted tier."
- "We’ve been burned by benchmark claims that don’t match our token mix—please include sequence length assumptions."
- "We need to be able to tell customers how data is handled; default retention is a no-go."

Risks / blockers
- Benchmark substantiation is gating the POC start (they want methodology, not just a chart).
- Multi-tenant story: they’re worried about end-customer prompts being stored; will likely need crisp retention/off-by-default guidance.
- Hosted rate limit anxiety for demo spikes; may accelerate Dedicated conversation earlier than ideal.

Next steps (owner)
- Avery
  - Send approved benchmark substantiation links + methodology notes (coordinate with Soojin for claim-safe language).
  - Share Dedicated starter pricing range + capacity planning assumptions for a spiky workload.
- Ethan
  - Provide a benchmark pack: model(s) tested, hardware, batching, sequence-length distribution, and how results map to their workload.
- Target outcome for next meeting
  - Agreement on success criteria for a 2–3 week POC (streaming success rate, p95 latency, cost envelope) + decide Hosted vs Dedicated for POC.
